items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: we had a rehearsal up in Skitch Henderson’s studio.

ctx.x: And that’s how I got Benny Goodman — before that I was with Benny Goodman. I played two years with him. We went to Las Vegas and other places. He played with symphonies sometimes and played jazz after that with his sextet. And he was very good to me. He fired everybody in the band at one time but myself. Because you know people don’t understand the man’s a genius, and he expected his men to play as well as he played. He expected that. And if you can’t satisfy him, you have to leave that’s all there is to it. And…

rehearse this, or what do you want to do fellas, you don’t do that. He just took his clarinet and played the [humms] played the melody and everything, and then he stopped all of a sudden, and started taking the clarinet apart and walking out. We said what’s wrong with this man? He walked out. And he stayed out [inaudible]. And so his valet came out and I said, “is this all?” He says, “yes, this is all.” He said, “don’t call me, we’ll call you” one of those things. So everybody started going out, packing up and…
